title: Kenshi has no TV camera, so we built an AI director that films our 24/7 stream. What we learned.
author: Designer_Pop_601
selftext:
We run a 24/7 stream where an AI plays the sandbox RPG Kenshi with a full squad. The game was made for a player looking at their own squad from above, so it has nothing like a TV camera. We ended up building a camera director that runs by itself.

A few things we learned along the way:

- Picking the shot is the easy part. Knowing when NOT to cut is harder. Early versions cut every time something moved and it was unwatchable.
- Variety has to be forced. Left alone, the director found one "safe" shot and used it for hours. Now it keeps track of what it showed recently and prefers whatever has rested the longest.
- Slow motion on the final blow of a fight did more for watchability than any other single change.

The clip shows three of the moves, a night tracking shot, a fly-by and a slow arc: https://youtube.com/shorts/Iieyn3ZOPDw

Happy to answer questions about what worked and what didn't. (The show is Kenshi Live Show if you want to see it running.)
